candidates.title: Civic monument repurposed as urban drone/military base
candidates.shift: A planned 250-foot triumphal arch monument in Washington DC is being redesigned mid-construction into a 'military complex' for launching drones and stationing snipers.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: extraordinary case of civic architecture converted into active military-drone infrastructure inside a capital city — could presage embedding drone-launch capability into ordinary urban buildings.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen reports Trump's Truth Social announcement that the DC triumphal arch design will now function as a military base with drones and snipers.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of civic/monumental architecture reclassified as active military infrastructure; if normalized, could blur symbolic public space and militarized urban infrastructure, affecting airspace/drone rules near commercial districts. Off-map, may eventually touch INFRASTRUCTURE/POLICY branch.
candidates.author: Tom Ravenscroft

candidates.title: Schools embedded in prison complexes
candidates.shift: A new educational facility is built as part of a larger prison complex, positioned to connect more to the city than to the prison, blurring civic and carceral real estate.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: strange juxtaposition — early example of mixed civic/carceral site programming that could inform how reentry-adjacent commercial space gets sited near correctional facilities.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily describes Educational Facility URSIKS built within a new Ljubljana prison complex, positioned along a road connecting it more to the city than the prison.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of blending institutional typologies (education + incarceration) at the site level; if this framing spreads, zoning categories for reentry-adjacent commercial corridors may need new definitions.
candidates.author: Valeria Silva

candidates.title: Women-only boarding house rethought for tight urban plots
candidates.shift: A new guesthouse in dense Indonesian residential fabric reworks the women-only boarding house typology for extreme spatial efficiency on an irregular trapezoidal lot.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: peripheral-geography case of gender-specific micro-housing efficiently packed into leftover urban plots — could inform small-format retail/infill use of odd lots in dense Asian cities.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily profiles Anir Guest House in Semarang, Indonesia, a women-only boarding house on an 11x25m trapezoidal plot.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of gender-specific micro-housing typology adapted to irregular infill lots; if such efficient-infill approaches spread, small-format retail/mixed-use could follow similar spatial-efficiency logic in dense Asian cities.
candidates.author: Pratik Mour

candidates.title: Retail floors as robot training ground
candidates.shift: Open datasets capturing human movement/interaction in stores are being built specifically to train mobile robots to navigate around shoppers and staff.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: signals a coming wave of store-floor robots (restocking, cleaning) needing behavioral data on human-robot coexistence; strange that store aisles are becoming machine training data.
candidates.evidence: arXiv paper introduces an open multimodal dataset of human activity combined with robot-guided movement in retail environments.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of stores becoming training environments for physical AI; if scaled, retailers may need to license/anonymize footage of shoppers for robot training, raising privacy and store-design questions.
candidates.author: Xiangrui Wang, Yuetong Wu, Jalen Beeman et al.

candidates.title: Autonomous rickshaws threaten informal transport labor
candidates.shift: Solar-assisted autonomous e-rickshaws are being piloted in Dhaka, potentially displacing millions of low-income informal drivers who support last-mile mobility.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: early physical-AI mobility case in the Global South that could presage disruption to gig/informal delivery labor pools retailers rely on for last-mile fulfillment.
candidates.evidence: Preprint describes a geofenced, solar-assisted autonomous rickshaw for Bangladesh, quantifying displacement risk to 1-2 million informal drivers in Dhaka.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from human-driven informal transit to autonomous fleets; if scaled, could ripple into last-mile delivery labor markets retailers use in dense emerging-market cities, with no insurance category yet for displaced workers.
candidates.author: Md Israfeel
